All `rosmium` functions operate on local files, and the format of each file is
determined from its **suffix**. This vignette describes the suffixes
recognised for OSM data (input and output of all main functions), and the
separate set of formats written by the `osmium_export()` function.

## Standard formats

OSM file formats are specified by one or two suffixes, such as `.osm.pbf` or
`.osc.gz`. Handling is delegated to `libosmium`, so every function accepting
or writing OSM files recognises the same set.

### Primary suffixes

The last format suffix (before any compression suffix) specifies the actual
file format:

| Suffix | Format |
| --- | --- |
| `.pbf` | Binary Protocol Buffer Format. The most compact and fastest format, and the usual choice (`.osm.pbf`). |
| `.xml` | OSM XML. |
| `.opl` | Object Per Line: a text format with one OSM object per line, convenient for line-based tools such as `grep`. |
| `.json` | OSM JSON. |
| `.o5m` | The compact binary `o5m` format. |
| `.o5c` | The `o5m` change-file variant, which may contain multiple versions of each object. |
| `.debug` | Human-readable debug dump of the data. |
| `.blackhole` | Output only: data are discarded. Useful for testing or timing. |
| `.ids` | A list of object IDs. |

### Secondary suffixes

A secondary suffix placed in front of a primary one describes the *content* of
the file, rather than its encoding:

| Suffix | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.osm` | Standard OSM data. On its own, `.osm` implies XML, so `x.osm` is equivalent to `x.osm.xml`. |
| `.osh` | History file, containing multiple versions of each object. XML by default (`x.osh`), or combined with another format (`x.osh.pbf`). |
| `.osc` | Change file, describing modifications to be applied to data. XML by default (`x.osc`), or combined with another format (`x.osc.opl`). |

Typical complete file names are therefore `.osm.pbf` (OSM data in PBF),
`.osm` (OSM XML), `.osh.pbf` (history in PBF), and `.osc` (XML change file).

### Compression

Files may additionally be compressed, by appending a compression suffix, such
as `.osm.bz2` or `.opl.gz`. Both `.gz` and `.bz2` are supported.

---

## Export formats

`osmium_export()` is different from other functions in that it converts OSM
data to geometry-bearing *features*, rather than writing another OSM file. The
formats written are therefore distinct from those above, and can generally not
be used as input to any subsequent `rosmium` functions.

| Format | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `geojson` | A single GeoJSON `FeatureCollection`. Can be read with packages like [`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/). |
| `geojsonseq` | Line-delimited GeoJSON sequence, with one feature per record. Better suited to very large outputs. |
| `text` | Plain text output, with one feature per line, suitable for loading into spatial databases and GeoPackage workflows. |
| `pg` | PostgreSQL `COPY` format, for bulk loading into PostGIS. |

### Specifying the format

The format may be given explicitly through the `output_format` parameter:

```{r}
#| label: export-format
#| eval: false
osmium_export (input, output = "roads.txt", output_format = "geojson")
```

Alternatively, if `output_format` is `NULL`, it is taken from the suffix of the
`output` file. The names `json`, `jsonseq`, and `txt` are accepted as aliases
for `geojson`, `geojsonseq`, and `text`, respectively. Format names are not
case-sensitive.

```{r}
#| label: export-suffix
#| eval: false
osmium_export (input, output = "roads.geojson") # GeoJSON
osmium_export (input, output = "roads.geojsonseq") # GeoJSON sequence
osmium_export (input, output = "roads.txt") # text
osmium_export (input, output = "roads.pg") # PostgreSQL COPY
```

If no `output` is given, results are returned as a character string and
`output_format` must be specified.

### Options

Further options of `osmium_export()` control which features and attributes are
written, irrespective of format: `geometry_types` (any of `"point"`,
`"linestring"`, and `"polygon"`), `keep_untagged`, `attributes` (such as
`"version,timestamp"`), `add_unique_id`, and a `config` file for tag
inclusion and exclusion rules. See `?osmium_export` for details.
